column10: Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92)

This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario b. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario a. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

column10: Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95)

A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92)

One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario c. A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario c. In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95)

column10: Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

column10: Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

column10: Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario a. To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

column149:
I did not like the way the options were written, they were either "I'm a material person and don't care about the environment, I only want comfort" or "I'm a very good citizen and do as I'm told". 
Here's the thing, not every city/town in Europe is London. Some of us live in smaller places, where the only bus stop is 30 minutes away from your house, and the bus ride to your place work takes almost an hour, and then you have to either take another bus or walk for an extra 30 minutes. 
Now, I'm no math expert, but I think that's pretty much 2 hours. Or, I can drive my car and be there in 25 minutes. If I drive my car, I save pretty much 3 hours that I can use for myself, because, and this might come as a surprise to you friends, people need to have spare time. 
I know for you it's very easy to picture the commoners spending 8 hours at work and 4 hours riding the bus to "save the planet", but that takes half the day, and we have to sleep too, you know? So at the end of the day, in your version of the ideal world, a person like me would end up having 4 hours to prepare my food, shower, enjoy some free time, go and get my groceries, etc. All that while the president of my country (which isn't very big), moves around in a private plane. 
But I have to share the washing machine with my neighbor. 
In your perfect world, a robot decides if I've been a good boy and deserve hot water, but India, the US and China can keep polluting everything. 
At the very least, I'm glad you're no longer even pretending to actually care about the well being of us, because that will make it easier for the people to realize the stuff you're trying to do, and, hopefully, stop you.

You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

column149: Presented options of the future look amazing, but I think they lack some forward thinking, especially the idea of a 15 minute city. I don't think it takes into account people with disabilities. In my country (Poland) it is already extremally difficutl for people with disabilities to access private buildings, cinemas, restaruants, etc. I myself am a person with a disability and a recent car owner, which has substantially helped with my independence and lvel of life. The 15 minute city idea is exciting on paper, but I don't think it is sustainable. As for the electric cars, I would love to be able to afford one, but I don't think we have now the technology that supports the transition from diesel/petrol to electric cars. I think those need at least another 10 yeats of development to be a reliable as "classic" cars and they also need to be much cheaper so the people with lower income can afford them.

You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. column10: Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95)

column10: Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

column10: Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92)

column10: Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91); Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92)

column10: Scenario c. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)

An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. You have solar panels integrated into the building and a battery system that allows you to store excess daily energy to consume at night. The generation system is slightly oversized, and in summer, you have a surplus of energy generated that is used at the community electrolyzer that generates and stores hydrogen. This hydrogen is later used in a highly efficient community cogeneration system (a.k.a. technology that produces electricity and thermal energy) to power a low-temperature district heating that provides the heating/cooling and hot water demand of the community. All these components could be controlled by an energy management system in which you can invest, not only to optimize its performance but also to allow you to trade energy between neighbors or with the energy provider.(ID93); Scenario b. You live in a new or highly refurbished passive house (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_house). In addition to having first-class facade, roof and window insulation, an intelligent and highly efficient heating/air conditioning system supplies the dwelling with your heating, cooling and hot water needs. An energy management system controls the heating/air conditioner system giving to it the potential to share energy with the neighbors building a “distributed district heating”. Moreover, you are very environmentally conscious so you prioritize saving energy with any kind of investment of money or time, and you are always willing to sacrifice some comfort when setting the thermostat temperature.(ID92); Scenario d. The city where you live has been re-designed in a way that all services are at foot distance (for example, following the idea of 15 mins cities - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_minute_city). A series of agreements between the government and companies, aligned with investments in behavior change from the citizens’ side, ensures that teleworking is mandatory at least three days a week. In your city, the number of vehicles is drastically reduced due to several incentives to embrace low-emissions mobility vehicles (e.g., bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, etc.) and facilities to take public transport. Indeed, a combination of public or private personal mobility, robotaxis (a.k.a. self-driving taxi or a driverless taxi) and electric public transport supply the rest of travel needs (inter and intra city). For these reasons, traffic jams are something from the past and the air is again breathable. Long distance transport of passengers and goods is only made using trains and the amount of travel by plane is drastically reduced to intercontinental travel.(ID95); Scenario a. One of the appliances you use occasionally (e.g. the oven for baking, the washing/drying machine, a drill or the vacuum cleaner) breaks down again. In order to contribute to the climate neutrality objectives, you decide not to buy a new piece of equipment for individual use but to propose its purchase to your community for shared and common use (and that way you can buy the highest energy efficiency option). To do this, you convince your entire building community to share these household appliances for common everyday use. Luckily, you have space in the basement to accommodate them and you propose to your community to adhere to this initiative when they have to replace their equipment and not before.(ID91)
